Bind an argument to state in the browser

Source: R/vue_bind.R
vue_bind.Rd

A component's argument given vue_bind() in place of a value follows state on the page, with no round trip to the server: a store's field, another component's value, the route. It is how a Vue application's components share a ref, for components that are each an application of their own – the page's UI state stays in the browser, and the server keeps the data and the decisions.

Usage

vue_bind(path)

Arguments

path

The state to follow: a string starting with $store, $inputs or $route.

Value

The path, classed "vue_bind", to give as an argument's value.

Details

Three kinds of state can be bound:

  • $store.<id>.<field>: a vue_store()'s state, both ways. The component follows the field, and when its user changes it – a dialog closed, a value picked – the field is set, so everything bound to it follows.

  • $inputs.<id>: the value another component reports as input$<id>, one way. In a module, the id is the namespaced one, in brackets: vue_bind(sprintf("$inputs['%s']", ns("size"))).

  • $route.<...>: the route of the page's vue_router(), one way: $route.path, $route.params.id.

A path goes on with .<name>, ['<name>'] or [<index>]. A component's value – what it reports as input$<id> – can be bound to a store alone: bound to something read-only, its user's change would be lost. A component drawn as markup (a dialog, a drawer, tabs, a collapse) can bind what its update_*() can set. An argument R reads to draw a component – a label, the choices – is an error.

The binding holds the argument from then on: update_*() of the field sets it, and through it the store; bound to $inputs or $route, the field keeps the update until what it follows changes again. With Shiny on the page, the component reports input$<id> as ever, so the server sees what the page did.

Acting in the browser needs nothing more: an on handler may be Vue's inline statement, as @click="..." in a template, which reaches the stores and whatever the component library installs on every component, as a message service – on = list(click = "$store.ui.open = true"), "$message('Saved')". A JS() handler runs with the component as this: this.$store.ui.open = true.

See also

vue_store() for state shared by components.

Examples

# A size picked in one component, followed by another
htmltools::tagList(
  vue_app(
    "size",
    htmltools::tags$select(
      `v-model` = "size",
      htmltools::tags$option("small"),
      htmltools::tags$option("large")
    ),
    data = list(size = "small"),
    input = "size"
  ),
  vue_app(
    "shown",
    htmltools::tags$span("Size: {{ size }}"),
    data = list(size = vue_bind("$inputs.size"))
  )
)
#> <div id="size" data-shiny-vue style="display: contents">
#>   <script type="text/x-template" data-shiny-vue-template><select v-model="size">
#>   <option>small</option>
#>   <option>large</option>
#> </select></script>
#>   <script type="application/json" data-shiny-vue-options>{"options":{"data":{"size":"small"}},"input":"size","evals":[]}</script>
#> </div>
#> <div id="shown" data-shiny-vue style="display: contents">
#>   <script type="text/x-template" data-shiny-vue-template><span>Size: {{ size }}</span></script>
#>   <script type="application/json" data-shiny-vue-options>{"options":{"data":{"size":null}},"bound":{"size":"$inputs.size"},"evals":[]}</script>
#> </div>

# A store both follow: the second sets it
htmltools::tagList(
  vue_store("ui", state = list(open = FALSE)),
  vue_app(
    "toggle",
    htmltools::tags$button(`@click` = "open = !open", "Toggle"),
    data = list(open = vue_bind("$store.ui.open"))
  ),
  vue_app("state", htmltools::tags$span("{{ $store.ui.open }}"))
)
#> <div id="ui" data-shiny-vue style="display: contents">
#>   <script type="text/x-template" data-shiny-vue-template><span hidden></span></script>
#>   <script type="application/json" data-shiny-vue-options>{"options":{"data":{"open":false}},"store":true,"evals":[]}</script>
#> </div>
#> <div id="toggle" data-shiny-vue style="display: contents">
#>   <script type="text/x-template" data-shiny-vue-template><button @click="open = !open">Toggle</button></script>
#>   <script type="application/json" data-shiny-vue-options>{"options":{"data":{"open":null}},"bound":{"open":"$store.ui.open"},"evals":[]}</script>
#> </div>
#> <div id="state" data-shiny-vue style="display: contents">
#>   <script type="text/x-template" data-shiny-vue-template><span>{{ $store.ui.open }}</span></script>
#>   <script type="application/json" data-shiny-vue-options>{"options":{"data":[]},"evals":[]}</script>
#> </div>
